1.5.1 Emergency Response Coordination Activities

The purpose of emergency response coordination activities is to coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations. The intent is for local response organizations to be made aware of the regulated substances at Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres, their quantities, the risks presented by the covered process, and the resources and capabilities at our facility to respond to an accidental release of a regulated substance. The emergency response coordination activities will consist of the following:
Coordinations will be completed at least annually. Additional coordinations will be made to account for changes at our facility that may affect the community emergency response plan.
Coordinations will include Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres emergency response plan, updated emergency contact information, and any other information necessary for developing and implementing the local emergency response plan.

Coordination activities will be appropriately documented. The coordination records will include the names of individuals involved and their contact information (phone number, email address, and organizational affiliations), dates of coordination activities, and nature of coordination activities.

The disclosure of information classified or restricted by the Department of Defense or other Federal agencies or contractors of such agencies is controlled by applicable laws,

This program is intended to meet the spirit and intent of the following regulations:
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2
Federal EPA Risk Management Program (RMP)  Title 40 CFR §68
California Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 8 CCR §5189
Federal Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 29 CFR §1910.119
Hereafter this program will be referred to as the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program.

This program is intended to be a living document. As such, the information, procedures, policies, and documentation that make up this program must be made easily accessible and updated as necessary. To accomplish this, Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has elected to use PSMWriter, software developed and distributed by Resource Compliance, Inc. This software will assist us with updating, maintaining, scheduling, and tracking RMP/PSM/CalARP related activities. 

1.1 BWC Shady Acres, Risk and Process Safety Management Program

This is to inform all interested persons, including employees, that Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has developed their unified RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This program has been prepared to address the risks involved in operating and maintaining the following process which have the presence of hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities: 
Process Name            -      Process Chemical          -      Process Quantity(lbs.)
Ammonia Storage           Anhydrous Ammonia             41,000

Our RMP/PSM/CalARP Program promotes overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. The program enables our facility to prevent the occurrence, and minimize the consequences, of significant releases of hazardous chemicals. Overall, the program is designed to prevent accidental fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and physical property damage.
Our company has many policies and procedures in place to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. We have: 
Prepared a unified program ba

sed on the PSM regulation to meet CalARP and RMP obligations as well
Organized the program so that it meshes closely with general business practices
Utilized PSMWriter software to ensure that all necessary employees have access to relevant information (SOPs, PHAs, audits, etc.)
The RMP/PSM/CalARP Program sets forth rules, procedures, and practices that will help our employees and neighbors protect themselves.

1.2 Process Description

1.2.1 Facility Overview

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres is a fertilizer storage and resale facility. The ammonia process operates as follows. Ammonia is supplied by a vendor into the ammonia storage tank. From there it is stored until a sale is made, at which time a Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres employee transfers ammonia from the storage tank into a smaller trailer-mounted nurse tank. The nurse tanks are towed by trucks off site for the fertilizer application.

1.2.2 Facility Location

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres is located at 15355 W Elkhorn Ave. Helm, CA 93627. The latitude and longitude of the storage tank is 36.480889, -120.070250. The process is located approximately 1.5 miles west of state highway 145 in a rural area surrounded by agricultural land.

1.2.3 Process Classification

The ammonia process at Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres consists of vessels, equipment, and valves which are interconnected by piping. As such, the system at Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres is treated as a single process.

1.3 General Accident Release & Chemical Specific Prevention Steps

1.3.1 General 

We inform our employees engaged in process operations of the dangers of an accidental release of anhydrous ammonia in annual safety meetings. During these meetings we also discuss preventative measures, such as evacuation, in order to be prepared for a release.
Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has also conducted an off-site consequence analysis of worst-case and alternative release s

cenarios for the ammonia process. These are for the purposes of informing the public in the event of an accidental release. The results of the analyses are reported in PSMWriter and hard copy binders. 

1.3.2 Anhydrous Ammonia

The ammonia process at the Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres facility is an integral part of the overall business and operates most of the year. It is extremely important that this process is maintained and operated in a safe and efficient manner. Management is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of an ammonia leak.

Our personnel monitor the ammonia process and keep active records of all procedures and transactions that pertain to ammonia.

1.4 Five Year Accident History

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has had no accidental release within the last five (5) years.

1.5 Emergency Action and Response Plan

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres emergency action and response program has been developed to satisfy the following requirements:
Cal/OSHAs Emergency Action Plan  Title 8 CCR §3220
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Emergency Action Plans  Title 29 CFR §1910.38
Cal/OSHAs Process Safety Management [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 8 CCR §5189(n)
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Process Safety Management [Emergency Planning and Response Requirements]  Title 29 CFR §1910.119(n)
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2 §5120.1-5120.2
USEPA Risk Management Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 40 CFR §68.90-96
California Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) [Emergency Response Plans and Procedures]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 1 §5030.7

1.5.2 Emergency Response Notification Exercises

At least once per calendar year, Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres will conduct an exercise of the facilitys emergency response notifications mechanism. The facility will record each notification exercise utilizing PSMWriter.

Alternatively, the facility may meet the notification requirements through other exercises conducted to meet other Federal, state or local requirements, provided that the necessary notification is performed. Additionally, if a notification is made in response to an accidental release, this would also satisfy the notification requirement.

1.6 Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has implemented many policies and procedures to promote overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. Nevertheless, Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres continually strives to improve in all areas, including safety.

By utilizing PSMWriter software, all necessary employees have access to every aspect of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This has improved Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres ability to communicate hazardous situations to employees and contractors. In addition, PSMWriter tracks all RMP/PSM/CalARP related events so that Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres management team can ensure that the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program is being implemented.

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has implemented all aspects of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. When a RMP/PSM/CalARP Program requirement is completed (i.e. mechanical integrity inspection, process hazard analysis, compliance audit, etc.) any specific action items related to that event are entered into PSMWriter, assigned a responsible person, and given a due date. Once the action item has been completed, the resolution can be documented using PSMWriter as well. A list of current or past due

action items can be accessed at any time by those with access to PSMWriter.

In addition to utilizing PSMWriter to create, schedule, track, and document events, Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres has also entered into a contract with Resource Compliance to obtain help with RMP/PSM/CalARP Program implementation.

Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres considers the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program a living document. It is an interactive framework that guides safe action for Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres employees, but allows for feedback and continual improvement. Through the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program Buttonwillow Warehouse Company Shady Acres will continue to maintain overall plant worker, public, and environmental safety.
